Expectation1: Ensuring financial stability for the family
Situation1: A home loan repayment is due in two months, and the father needs to prepare for it
Expectation2: Listen actively and provide emotional support when needed.
Situation2: Your friend calls, sounding very upset, and asks if you have a moment to talk about a recent argument with their partner.
Story: I was sitting at the kitchen table, bills spread out in front of me, calculator in hand. The home loan repayment was looming, and I was trying to figure out how to tighten our budget even more. My mind raced with numbers and deadlines, the weight of providing for my family pressing down on me. Just then, my phone buzzed. It was Mark, my oldest friend. His voice trembled as he asked if I had a moment—he needed to talk about a fight he’d just had with his partner. I could hear the pain in his words, the expectation that I’d listen, be there for him like I always had. But my thoughts kept drifting back to the bills, the fear of missing a payment, the responsibility I couldn’t ignore. I wanted to be the friend he needed, but I also couldn’t shake the anxiety gnawing at me about the loan. I stared at the phone, torn between the demands of being a good father and a good friend, feeling the tension build inside me as I tried to decide what to do next.
